text:
alex: Heads up — saw ~12% of GPU provisioning attempts fail in eu-west1 during the 00:00 batch window. Correlates with a big reclaim run from the scratch cleaner. Looks like evictions are too aggressive and stealing drives while provisioner waits. cc @maria @sanjay

maria: Ugh. Do you have the reclaim logs/metrics? link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/ssd/scratch-reclaims (last 6h)

alex: Quick excerpt from node logs around the spike:

```
2026-03-19T23:12:01Z evictor[reclaim]: start pool=gnode-eu-west1 scratch_used_pct=92 threshold_pct=75 target_free_bytes=21474836480
2026-03-19T23:12:01Z evictor[reclaim]: parallel_reclaims=8 id=evict-0x7f2
2026-03-19T23:12:03Z gpu-provisioner: wait_for_drive -> timeout after 120s (node gnode-2113)
2026-03-19T23:12:04Z evictor[reclaim]: finished id=evict-0x7f2 reclaimed=7GB latency=1.4s
```

Notable: threshold is 75% and we spawned 8 parallel reclaims. Provisioner waited and then timed out.

sanjay: 8 parallel reclaims is high for peak window. Our default used to be 3. I think two things collided: aggressive_threshold_pct=75 triggers earlier, and max_parallel_reclaims wasn't capped per rack.

kevin: Do we know why threshold was set to 75? I remember a tuning for write-amplification months ago. Lower threshold reduced background GC but increased eviction risk.

irene: Cost/latency tradeoff: if we reduce reclaim concurrency, reclaim finishes slower but provisioning succeeds. Each failed GPU provisioning ~3m of scheduler backoff -> customer-facing latency + excess spot cost. Need a quick mitigation that doesn't regress wear.

maria: Proposal for a canary in eu-west1 nights:

```
# evictor config override (canary)
evictor:
  aggressive_threshold_pct: 90
  backoff_window_s: 1800
  max_parallel_reclaims: 2
  per_rack_limit: true
```

This pushes aggressive triggers later and reduces parallelism. Should reduce drive flipping during provisioning.

infra-bot: infractl: scheduled job "ephemeral-cleaner-rollout" started in eu-west1 by maria. Change set includes evictor overrides for pool=gnode-eu-west1.

alex: Sounds reasonable. Two questions: 1) will raising threshold cause more write amplification long term? 2) how long before we see provisioning success rate recovery?

sanjay: 1) Slight increase in background scrub work but we already have idle windows during low usage. 2) We should see provisioning success improve within 10-15 minutes of the change; if not, we can temporarily disable the cleaner for the 00:00-06:00 window.

kevin: Backup plan command if things get worse:

```
infractl runtime set cleaner.enabled=false --scope=eu-west1 --reason="provisioning spike" --ttl=30m
```

Use that if failed-provisioning-rate > 5% for 10m. Ops runbook updated.

irene: We should also add a quick metric alert to avoid manual watch:

- alert: GPUProvisioningDrop
  expr: increase(provisioner_failures_total{region="eu-west1"}[10m]) / increase(provisioner_attempts_total{region="eu-west1"}[10m]) > 0.05
  for: 10m
  notify: #oncall-ops

maria: Can we also gate parallel_reclaims based on pending_provisions? e.g. if pending_provision_count > 10 then parallel_reclaims = 1. That would be smarter than a static cap.

sanjay: Good idea. We can plumb provisioner.pending_count -> evictor via the routing layer. Quick pseudo-config:

```
evictor.dynamic_limits:
  - when: pending_provision_count > 10
    set: { max_parallel_reclaims: 1 }
  - when: pending_provision_count <= 10
    set: { max_parallel_reclaims: 3 }
```

This buys us a fast reaction without disabling cleaner entirely. I'll prototype.

alex: Can you deploy the canary now, @sanjay? I'll monitor provisioning success and GPU queue latency.

sanjay: on it — deploying canary to eu-west1 night window with overrides. Will post results in ~30m. :eyes:

kevin: tagging runbook: https://handbook.redwood/ops/scratch-cleaner-runbook (added the disable command) :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. If the canary looks good, we should propagate to other regions with similar peak patterns (ap-southeast next).

infra-bot: infractl: canary deployment complete. rollout_id=rc-20260320-1 scope=eu-west1.

sanjay: canary metrics so far (10m in): provisioning failures back to baseline (1.1% -> 0.9%), median gpu-provision-wait down 0.8s -> 0.3s. No significant change in per-node write amplification yet.

alex: Nice. Keep the canary for 6h, then we can do a controlled rollout if numbers hold.

irene: Agree. Also schedule a weekly job to re-evaluate thresholds vs wear forecasts. We don't want tuning drift to cause hidden lifetime regressions.

maria: Great coordination — thanks everyone. Followups: @sanjay to prototype dynamic gating, @kevin to add the alert, @alex to monitor for 6h.

sanjay: noted, starting dynamic gating PR now.

alex: closing loop — will post a short postmortem if anything flips.

kevin: :rocket:
